Subject: Remuneration bracket revision & regional scaling proposal

Hi team,

Attached is draft v3 of the remuneration brackets and the regional scaling proposal we discussed in last week's comp calibration sync. High level:

- Purpose: tighten leveling cutpoints for IC and manager bands, and introduce a 3-tier geo multiplier (Tier A / B / C) tied to localized cost-of-labor indices.
- Impact: expected uplift on offers for select AP/EMEA hubs and a modest downward adjustment in lower-cost LATAM locales. Net budget impact for new hires this FY is estimated at ~2.1% of base hiring run-rate (see workbook).
- Headcount approvals: model assumes existing reqs for Q2 remain unchanged; any uplift >5% per role will require manager-level approval + HR sign-off.

Please review the following specific asks:
1) Marissa — validate operational offer language and identify any legal flags (we need neutral phrasing for variable multipliers).
2) Laura — confirm market anchors for L4-L6 managers; I pulled Mercer and Lightcast comps into sheet tab "Anchors".
3) Jonas — sanity-check the forecasted budget delta by org and the proposed thresholds for automatic manager approval.
4) Neha — recommend adjustments for our APAC hiring playbook.

I also looped in David Ramos from Mercer for a quick external check; he sent a short note and a delta file (see his message below).

Attachments: 2027-Q1-geo-benchmarks.xlsx (workbook), rem_bracket_draft_v3.pdf (narrative).

Thanks — aiming to lock this for the 10 Mar exec HR review.

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan

Thanks Tessa — quick read-through this morning. A few inline notes: 

> - introduce a 3-tier geo multiplier (Tier A / B / C) tied to localized cost-of-labor indices.

I like the simplicity of 3 tiers. Suggest we map Tier A to top 15% of US metros by total comp (SF/NY/BOS/SEA), Tier B next 35%, Tier C everything else. For clarity we should include a short FAQ on how we treat remote employees who live outside their hiring manager's market.

> - model assumes existing reqs for Q2 remain unchanged; any uplift >5% per role will require manager-level approval + HR sign-off.

Agree on requiring approvals but propose the threshold be 7% for IC roles (to avoid over-signaling on small rounding changes) and keep 5% for manager roles. Also flag: relocation and sign-on buckets need explicit carve-outs.

One open item: the anchor table in tab "Anchors" shows Lightcast medians significantly higher for L5 engineers in LATAM than Mercer — can we reconcile the data sources before we finalize anchors?

If helpful I can run a short summary deck for the exec HR review (10 slides) — I can have that by Thu EOD.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Total Rewards
Redwood Inference

Hi Tessa/Laura — thanks for sharing. Quick notes from the Mercer side after a brief pass: 

- The Tier A/B/C segmentation aligns with our proposed market segmentation methodology; however, for Tier B we recommend splitting the band by "gateway cities" vs. secondary metros (this reduces abrupt offer jumps for employees in commuting zones).
- On sample sizes: for LATAM L4-L6 the Mercer sample is thinner; we've attached a delta CSV for roles where the underlying job-mapping confidence was <70%. Please treat those anchors as provisional.
- We've also generated a locality index (column L) you can drop into your workbook; it smooths short-term volatility by using a 12-month rolling mean.

Link to short summary: https://mercer-analytics.com/reports/redwood-q1-locality-summary (password: Redwood2027)

Team — thanks for the fast turnaround. Summary and decisions after reading David's delta: 

1) Anchors: Use Mercer as primary anchor, Lightcast medians will be used only where Mercer confidence <70% and after Laura's reconciliation.
2) Thresholds: adopt 7% uplift threshold for ICs, 5% for manager roles, carve-outs for relocation and sign-on.
3) Tiers: implement Tier A/B/C as proposed; Jonas to add "gateway city" smoothing for Tier B (reduce cliffing).
4) Budget: finance impact updated to +2.4% after Mercer adjustments — Jonas will update the Q2 hiring forecast.
5) Exec deck: Laura to prepare a 10-slide summary for the 10 Mar review; include clear ask slide with recommended approval matrix.
6) Ops: Marissa to prepare language updates for offer templates and recruiter scripts; target implementation for any new reqs posted after 1 Apr.

Next steps & owners: 
- Jonas Weber: update forecast + add gateway smoothing (due: Fri 5 Mar).
- Laura Bennett: reconcile Lightcast vs Mercer anchors and finalize slides (due: Thu 4 Mar EOD).
- Marissa Cole: draft offer language and recruiter FAQ (due: Mon 8 Mar).
- Neha Kapoor: review APAC adjustments and confirm any regional exceptions (due: Mon 8 Mar).

I'll present the executive ask on 10 Mar. If anything material changes after Laura's reconciliation we will escalate before the review.

Thanks — Tessa
